SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION:  • 1094 cm⁻¹ strong band matches aryl C–F stretching, present only in molecule 4 (fluoro-substituted phenol).  
• 506 cm⁻¹ medium band corresponds to aryl C–Br stretch, again unique to molecule 4 which contains a Br atom.  
• 1266 cm⁻¹ intense band is typical C–O stretching of a phenolic O–H group, consistent with the phenol functionality in candidate 4.  
• 1598 cm⁻¹, 1175 cm⁻¹ and 1213 cm⁻¹ bands are characteristic aromatic C=C and C–H in-plane bends, expected for a mono-hydroxy, di-halo substituted benzene ring.  
• Multiple out-of-plane/halogen modes at 672, 636 and 728 cm⁻¹ fit the presence of two different heavy halogens (Br and F) on the aromatic ring.  
• No strong aliphatic C–H stretches are expected; observed 3073 cm⁻¹ (aromatic C–H) and weaker 2972 cm⁻¹ are acceptable.  
Taken together, only candidate 4 (Oc1ccc(Br)cc1F) simultaneously explains the observed C–F, C–Br and phenolic C–O signatures.
